correctness.rationale: The fixed-positive-mutation Fermi birth–death chain is irreducible and its stationary weights are analytic near δ=0 by the product formula. The stationary mean drift differentiates to (1−μ)∑π₀(k)k(N−k)Δₖ/[4μN(N−1)]. For N=4 the neutral detailed-balance ratios π₀(1)/π₀(0)=8μ/(1+μ) and π₀(2)/π₀(1)=3(1+5μ)/[4(1+2μ)], with reflection symmetry, give the stated probabilities. Direct leave-one-out payoffs give the gaps c(u−9)/9, c(−u+2v−9)/9, c(−2v+3w−9)/9. The weighted gap sum is 4cμ[(w−9)+μ(2v+2w−u−27)]/[(1+3μ)(1+11μ)], verifying the slope. At μ=1/2, c=1, u=2, w=9 it gives (2v−11)/780 and the two stated signs. For n=2 the r(1) term in the gap is proportional to N−2k; neutral drift weights are reflection symmetric, so that term cancels. The μ↓0 slope limit is c(w−9)/12; no uniform remainder or sign for all δ follows. These are exact analytic rechecks; the frozen script was inspected, not executed.
